answer: The registry mails each new seat a sealed token holding a signing quill, and the ivory seal breaks if the case is opened; every epoch that seat must send a signed pulse within a narrow window, and one token may back only one identity. Clones copy freely, but a seal cannot: k fake seats need k tokens delivered to k distinct addresses, each leaving a postal trail fraud teams can trace and refuse. A shared device fails too: the token countersigns one pulse at a time and rejects a second identity, so forgery costs track real shipping and interception risk rather than cheap virtual machines.
